findings.reason: §6 would ship a base arm that cannot fail and re-implement a shipped feature; the plan must re-aim at the cadence-loop path or delete the section.
findings.text: §6's whole change ("`reckon crew admit --once` emits one JSON document per pass naming each queued run it considered and its verdict with the detail admission-verdicts records") is already implemented: the `--once` option has existed since commit `8514b9773` (2026-10-12, ten days before §6's 2026-10-22 report), `admit_once` already builds `result["verdicts"]` (`queue_admission.py:1048`) whose rows carry `verdict="refused"` with the refusal's own `failure` detail (`queue_admission.py:1247`, row shape `_verdict_row` at `:863`), and `crew_admit` already emits the whole result as JSON (`crew_run_commands.py:3496`); §6's "Done when" ("On the base commit the pass prints nothing, so the test fails there") is therefore false for `--once` — the silent case is the *bare* verb, whose loop discards every pass's result at `queue_admission.py:1355` and returns only `{"passes": passes}` at `:1361`, which is exactly the invocation nova-47 ran

findings.reason: an implementer following the cited line puts the stacking exception in the reporter instead of the enforcer, and the ScopeConflict nova-47 saw would still be raised.
findings.text: §5 cites "the scope fence in `reckon/crew/node.py` (the refusal near line 1559)", but line 1559 is only the disposition branch that *reports* unintegrated work inside `claim_disposition` (`node.py:1500`); the refusal is composed and raised at `dispatch_claims.py:1696` by `_raise_repository_scope_conflict` (`dispatch_claims.py:1567`), which consumes `claim.disposition_reason`

findings.reason: the honest change is one line of emission on the loop path plus a bound stated in the help text at `crew_run_commands.py:3482`, not a second record of the same verdicts.
findings.text: §6 adds a per-pass JSON document "with the detail admission-verdicts records" as a new emission path, while the same pass already writes precisely that row set to `admission-verdicts.jsonl` through `_record_pass_verdicts` (`queue_admission.py:922`, log name at `:59`, write at `:959`), and adds `--once` (`crew_run_commands.py:3477`) which already exists; the section says nothing about why the existing flag and the existing log cannot serve, nor that the real gap is the loop path at `queue_admission.py:1355`

findings.reason: an unnamed fourth ancestry helper forks a mechanism with three owners and guarantees the three drift; naming the owner is a one-line change to §5's Change paragraph.
findings.text: §5 needs two mechanisms it does not place: an ancestry test for "the dispatch's base is that run's chain tip", which three existing owners already provide (`reckon/crew/merge.py:538` `_is_ancestor`, `reckon/crew/velocity.py:706` `_is_ancestor`, `reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:2389` `_revision_is_ancestor`), and a place to "record the stacking on both runs", whose owner is the pointer writer `reckon/crew/runs.py` (`_mutate_pointer`, reached from `queue_admission.py:770` `_write_pointer`)

findings.reason: §5's "Done when" asserts dispatch admits and refuses on the right base but never asserts the registry agrees, so the two readings of the same claim would disagree silently.
findings.text: §5 changes the claim decision `claim_disposition` (`node.py:1500`) but names only one of its two consumers; the second, `_live_scope_claims` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:932`), builds the registry a worker and `crew observe` read, and its own docstring says it deliberately carries "the same per-pointer disposition the dispatch scope check takes", so a stacked admission that changes binding in the enforcer but not here leaves the registry reporting the holder's paths as binding while dispatch admits over them; the other consumer is `_repository_scope_claims` (`dispatch_claims.py:286`, 267), which also feeds `refuse_widen_scope_conflicts` (`dispatch_claims.py:1714`) and every call site in `dispatch.py:1920`, `dispatch.py:2567`, `dispatch_plan.py:1122`

findings.reason: a section that adds to these families must say in its own text what it retires, merges, or why nothing can be; for §6 the true answer is that nothing needs adding, which is itself the plan change.
findings.text: public_definitions 2012, cli_options 400, mcp_views 19, refusal_families 23: §6 adds `--once` to `cli_options` without naming anything it retires or merges (and without recording that the option already exists), and §5 adds a refusal family ("promoting the holder while its descendant is live is refused naming the descendant") plus new pointer state on both runs without naming a refusal it retires or merges

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — neither section adds a module; §5 extends the existing deep module `claim_disposition` (`reckon/crew/node.py:1500`), which already hides process liveness, worktree inspection and integration-ref ancestry behind one call, and §6 extends one existing verb.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 adds a fourth ancestry test beside `merge.py:538`, `velocity.py:706` and `promotion_scope.py:2389`, and names neither the pointer writer that must record the stacking (`reckon/crew/runs.py`) nor the second consumer of the claim decision it changes (`reckon/crew/runs.py:932`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2012, cli_options 400, mcp_views 19, refusal_families 23; §6 adds a CLI option without naming what it retires or merges (or saying that the option already exists), and §5 adds a refusal family and new pointer fields without naming a refusal that is retired or merged.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6 proposes to create `reckon crew admit --once` and its per-request verdict document, both of which already exist in `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3477` and `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1048`/`:1247`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §6 adds a second emission path for admission verdicts beside the verdict log the same pass already writes, and re-declares a flag that exists, with no statement of why the existing flag and log cannot be used.
